summary: Describes two ways to route voice messages using a telephone number. The complete service uses the VPIM directory to look up an email address and confirm it belongs to the intended recipient. A simpler fallback, described as send-and-pray, uses only ENUM and ordinary DNS mail routing to deliver messages.

eli5.summary: You only know a friend's phone number but want to leave them a voice note over email. This memo shows two ways to find the right mailbox, one careful and one that just hopes for the best.

questions: route voice messages by telephone number
what is send and pray voice messaging
how does enum route voice messages
subtitle: Two ways to deliver a voice message to someone when all you know is their phone number.

tldr.problem: Voice messaging is addressed by telephone number, but Internet mail needs an email address.
tldr.mechanism: The complete service uses ENUM to find a VPIM directory and LDAP to fetch the verified email address. The basic send-and-pray service uses only ENUM rewrite rules to build an address and ordinary DNS MX routing to deliver it.
tldr.outcome: Senders can route voice messages from a phone number today with the basic service, with no guarantee the address is valid, and use the complete service where a directory exists. A later RFC 6118 updates this one.

today: RFC 4238 is a Proposed Standard from October 2005 and is updated by RFC 6118.

sections.title: Design Goals
sections.content:
RFC 4238 profiles two ways to route voice messages by telephone number. The most complete service uses ENUM to find the VPIM directory, then LDAP to get the VPIM-specific email address. The basic send-and-pray service uses only ENUM and MX records, and leaves final delivery to the routing system of the recipient's domain.

The basic mechanism may be used even when a directory exists, for example when LDAP queries are not possible for disconnected mobile terminals or because of firewall or security policy. It aims to need minimal configuration and no content processing: a simple rule can send all inbound VPIM messages to one system, while FAX, SMS or other telephone-addressed messages go elsewhere.

A timing goal is that directory discovery and query fit the response expectations of telephone networks: a two-second response 95% of the time. The mechanisms should also extend to other store-and-forward, telephone-number addressed messaging.
sections.eli5: There are two ways to find a mailbox from a phone number: a careful lookup, and a quick guess. Both should be fast and simple to set up.

sections.title: The Complete Service
sections.content:
For the complete service, the sending client SHOULD use ENUM to find the VPIM directory, then query it for the email address. The service is registered as E2U+VPIM:LDAP (URI type LDAP:).

The directory is found by querying for the VPIMDIR service on the recipient's number, using the DNS query name built as described in RFC 3761. The number may include sub-address digits. The answer is one or more NAPTR records holding LDAP URLs. VPIMDIR servers should be deployed redundantly, and NAPTR weights can give two servers the same preference or different shares of the load.

The client SHOULD then issue an LDAP query for vPIMrFC822Mailbox. That address SHOULD be used for both the RFC 822 To: field and the SMTP RCPT command, as described in RFC 4237.
sections.eli5: First you look up which phone book to use, then you ask that phone book for the exact mailbox to write on the envelope.

sections.title: The Basic Service
sections.content:
The basic service uses NAPTR rewrite rules to build a VPIM email address mechanically, with no directory. It is registered as E2U+VPIM:Mailto: (URI type Mailto:). The address SHOULD show that the message is VPIM in its domain name part, to help the recipient's mail routing.

There is no assurance that the constructed address is valid or belongs to the intended recipient. With no information about the recipient's capabilities, senders SHOULD use only the media and content types of the VPIM V2 profile.

Between domains, routing looks like ordinary email: the sender looks up the MX record for the domain and forwards the message. No infrastructure changes are required.

Inside the recipient's domain, routing is informational and is the domain's own business. A directory-enabled router can use the local part to find an internal address, as in +12145551212@sp.net. Alternatively, a gateway can send all voice messages to one system by matching a VPIM prefix on the domain, as in +12145551212@VPIM.sp.net.
sections.eli5: In the quick way, you build an address from the phone number by following a recipe. Mail gets to the right building, and the building's mailroom figures out the rest.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Little is disclosed to the sender beyond what email already reveals. Probing for valid addresses is the same as sending test messages and waiting for a non-delivery notice.

The main risks are these:

  • Unsolicited bulk email: turning phone numbers into routable email addresses lets bulk mailers target many recipients when only numbers are known or guessed.
  • DNS-based attacks: both services trust the DNS. A compromised DNS can send messages to a malicious address or point clients at a rogue LDAP server. DNSSEC substantially reduces the risk, but it does not protect against the LDAP service being compromised on its own.
  • Malicious redirection and denial of service: a bad or removed record can send clients to the wrong place or take away access.
sections.eli5: If someone tampers with the phone book or the recipe, your message can go to the wrong place. Locks on the phone book help, and so does knowing that spammers might guess numbers.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: The specification registers the E2U+VPIM and E2U+Voice services under the rules of RFC 3761 and the definitions in this document.
sections.eli5: The names of the two lookup services are written in an official list so everyone uses the same ones.
